- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast windows, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast peaks by 5–10%.
- After a significant price spike, model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward; apply a “cool-down” factor (e.g., reduce next 3–5 periods by 2–5% from peak).
- When sentiment is neutral or flat (all 0.00), model exhibits high volatility and overconfidence; dampen forecast variance by 15–25%.
- Mean reversion is underutilized; if price deviates >15% from 30-day moving average, adjust forecast toward average with decay factor (e.g., 0.85 per period).
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging true trends; if true outcome shows rapid reversal within 5–7 days, reduce forecast weight for later periods by 20–30%.
- No sentiment data available in examples — if sentiment later becomes positive, model should adjust upward; if negative, adjust downward — but only if sentiment changes >0.30.
